doc.description:
Opt-in STM32F4 ChibiOS AP hang watchdog. Bench validation is required before flight: a reset is not an in-flight recovery strategy.
main_chibios starts IWDG after application initialization. The actuator task supplies a heartbeat; only completion of the AP periodic and event pass consumes it and reloads IWDG. No timer, interrupt or separate thread feeds the watchdog. It does not verify sensor freshness or control validity.
The nominal timeout is 2000 ms at the nominal LSI frequency. Actual reset timing varies with the MCU's LSI tolerance. Cold-start initialization is not covered. IWDG cannot be stopped once started. Shutdown, sleep, firmware upload and debugger behavior must be checked on the real board.
DEBUG_VECT named watchdog reports x = RCC reset flags shifted right 24 bits (bit 5 is IWDG), y = watchdog started (0 or 1), z = nominal timeout in ms. Flags are captured before halInit, then cleared for the next boot. A bootloader may modify those flags before the application sees them.
This module does not restore mission state or change throttle/arming policy. Hardware outputs during reset and bootloader execution are not controlled by this module. Hard-fault recovery is not supported together with this module. See doc/watchdog_adam.md for bench acceptance checks.

define.name: WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_MS
define.description: Nominal IWDG timeout in ms (250 to 8192 at 32 kHz LSI)
